[{"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/165
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`entire graph stats` was reported as (a) pegging the machine and (b) printing a report when the
user wants one number. Both are fixed, and the fix for the weak part of the estimate turned out
to be the same change as half the performance fix.

## Before / after, on the reported directory

The machine that reported this has **1.9 GB across 3,323 `*.jsonl`** under one project
(`~/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv`). Wall clock and peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time -l`,
two to three runs per cell:

| `--since` | before | after, cold (`--no-cache`) | after, warm memo |
|---|---|---|---|
| `30d` (the default) | **60.1–70.0 s**, 99–101 MB | 14.9–15.4 s, 108 MB | **0.34–0.64 s**, 191–259 MB |
| `all` | 49.6–61.6 s, 99–101 MB | 13.5–13.8 s, 110–112 MB | 0.64–1.00 s, 259–264 MB |
| `1d` | 39.3 s, 101 MB | 3.1–4.1 s, 45–46 MB | 0.28–0.65 s, 153–233 MB |

The default run is **~180x faster warm and ~4x faster cold**. Peak RSS is the honest cost: the
warm path holds the memo (6.6 MB gzipped on disk) in memory, so peak rises from ~100 MB to
~190–264 MB. `--no-cache` keeps it at ~110 MB.

Where the time went, and why it is gone:

* **Half of it was system time, not parsing.** The old estimator priced its counterfactual by
  resolving the top-hit file of every credited graph call, which ran two regexes over the whole
  tool result and then an `os.OpenRoot` plus a per-component `Lstat` for up to 72 path candidates.
  Baseline runs spent **16–35 s in `sys`**; the new ones spend **0.7–1.0 s**. Replacing the model
  deleted that work outright.
* **`--since` was applied after the scan.** `--since 1d` JSON-parsed all 1.9 GB and then threw it
  away in the per-session filter. Candidates are now pruned by file mtime first: `1d` parses 683
  of 3,323 files, `7d` 2,325, `30d` 3,322, `all` 3,323. (Pruning is per *session*, so a project
  with a handful of long-lived sessions — this one has ten — prunes little at 30d and a lot at 1d.
  The memo is what makes the wide windows fast.)
* **Nothing was cached across runs.** Transcripts are append-mostly, so a per-file summary memo
  makes repeat runs near-instant.

## What is measured and what is estimated

**Estimated — and it stays labelled as such.** The counterfactual cannot be observed. The `~` is
in the default line for that reason, and the full model text is printed under `--verbose` and
carried verbatim in `savings_model` in the JSON.

**What changed is that both of the model's prices are now measured**, per session, from the
session's own transcript:

```
graph cost/call         = locate result bytes      / locate results observed
exploration cost/call   = exploration result bytes / exploration results observed
saving per substitution = max(0, exploration cost/call - graph cost/call)
tokens saved            = credited locate calls x saving per substitution / 4
```

The only assumption left is the 1:1 substitution ratio, and it is not invented: a paired A/B
benchmark of this tool measured **0.980 exploration calls displaced per graph call**. It is
carried as 1:1, which understates. The old model guessed *both* inputs — the counterfactual was
"one whole file", sized by whatever file the result happened to name, falling back to the repo's
median tracked-file size — and on this directory that produced **82.9 M tokens** where the
measured-input model produces **46 k**. The estimator no longer touches the repository's
filesystem at all.

**Consistency check against our own benchmark.** This repo's paired A/B puts the effect at
COST +2.49 %, CI [−6.83, +11.18], median negative, with graph output *larger* per call than the
baseline's. The new model on ten real sessions:

| sessions | per-call delta (exploration − graph, bytes) |
|---|---|
| 4 positive | +665, +1131, +1177, +1411 |
| 4 negative | −118, −525, −3641, −4095 |
| 2 | no locate calls at all |

Mean per-call delta is **negative** (−424 B/call); 4 of 8 sessions with locate calls saved
nothing. Aggregate: 45,963 tokens against 33.5 B billed. That sits inside a CI that straddles
zero and reproduces the "graph output is often larger per call" finding rather than contradicting
it — the model reports **0 for a session where the graph cost more than it displaced, and that is
not floored away at the total**, which is a sum of per-session results.

## New default output

```
$ entire graph stats --repo .
[entire-graph] ~45,963 tokens saved
```

One line. Green on a terminal; plain text under `NO_COLOR`, a pipe or a redirect, via the same
`shouldUseColor` rules the rest of the binary uses. The two degenerate cases stay one line too
("no coding-agent session transcripts for this repo yet…", "no sessions in this window…").

**`--verbose` restores the full report** — repo/sessions/window lines, the graph-calls-vs-
exploration line, both tables, billed tokens, the new measured per-call costs, and the wrapped
model text.

**`--format json` is unchanged in shape.** `scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh` reads
`estimated_savings_est_tokens` and `estimated_savings_pct_of_session_tokens` on every prompt
render, so keys are only ever added: `transcripts_considered`, `transcripts_from_cache`,
`graph_locate_calls`, `graph_locate_returned_bytes`, `graph_bytes_per_locate_call`,
`exploration_bytes_per_call`, `sessions_with_positive_savings`, `substitution_ratio`.
`median_tracked_file_bytes` is retired but stays in the contract, always 0.
`TestStatsJSONContractKeepsEveryPublishedKey` asserts the 29 previously published keys against a
golden list, and `--verbose` is asserted not to change the JSON.

## Accuracy audit (independent of the model)

* **Cross-transcript double counting — real, and measured.** Across the 3,316 real transcripts,
  **215 `tool_use` ids and 168 usage-bearing `message.id`s appear in more than one transcript of
  the same session** (Claude Code replays a forked subagent's history into the new file; zero
  collisions cross session boundaries). The old code billed each of those twice, in both call
  counts and bytes. Sessions are now assembled from per-call and per-message identities, so one
  API call counts once however many transcripts carry it.
* **Tool-result pairing is strictly file-local** — 0 of 155,343 results pair with a `tool_use` in
  a different file — which is what makes a per-file summary a faithful unit and the memo sound.
* **Per-call prices divide by results observed, never calls issued**, so a call whose result never
  reached the transcript cannot deflate a price.
* **`mulDiv`** replaces `a*b/c`. The product already reaches ~10^13 on real volumes and would
  silently wrap int64; it is now exact via `bits.Mul64`/`bits.Div64`, saturating instead of
  wrapping, with the `hi >= c` boundary pinned (`bits.Div64` *panics* at `hi == c`).
* **`roundTo`** uses `math.Round` instead of an int64 truncation that rounded negatives toward
  zero and was undefined outside int64 range.
* **Determinism**: two runs over an unchanged directory are byte-identical, asserted for the
  default text, `--verbose` and JSON.
* The memo's key is file *identity* (path + size + mtime) salted with the summary schema, the CLI
  version and the running executable's own size and mtime — a rebuilt binary misses rather than
  trusting a summary written by different parsing code. A missing, truncated, corrupt or
  foreign-schema memo is treated as empty and recomputed, never served. Entries for transcripts
  no longer on disk are dropped each run, driven by the full candidate list so a narrow `--since`
  does not evict what a later `--since all` wants.

## Tests

19 new tests; every behaviour change has one that fails on a compile-clean revert (14 reverts
applied, built, and run: mtime prune, session-scoped prune, cross-transcript tool_use dedup,
cross-transcript usage dedup, terse default, locate-only pricing, `roundTo`, `mulDiv`, colour
gating, JSON contract, memo lookup, memo key, memo salt, memo pruning). 20 mutants applied to the
new decision helpers in both directions; 15 killed, 5 survived and were adjudicated — one was a
genuine escape (`hi >= c` → `hi > c`, a `bits.Div64` panic path) and is now killed by
`mulDiv(1<<32, 1<<32, 1)`; the other four are equivalent mutants with proofs in the review notes
(`a <= 0`→`a < 0` and `displaced <= x`→`<` differ only where both branches return 0;
`||`→`&&` in the savings precondition is unreachable because `mulDiv` is total; dropping
`cutoff.IsZero()` is equivalent because no `time.Time` is `Before` the zero time).

Tests changed rather than deleted where they encoded the old shape:
`TestStatsTextOutputCarriesRatioAndCaveat` now drives `--verbose` (that is where the report went)
and additionally asserts the new measured-per-call line; the missing-dir and empty-dir tests were
updated to the new one-line wording; `TestStatsSavingsModelMath` and
`TestStatsSavingsFlooredAtZeroWhenGraphCostsMore` were rewritten around the new arithmetic; the
status-line fixture's exploration results were enlarged, because the badge exists to show a
session where exploration cost more per call than the graph did.

Deleted with the code they covered: `TestStatsMedianFallbackWhenTopHitUnresolvable`,
`TestStatsFileSizeStaysInsideTheSelectedRepository` and `stats_mount_windows_test.go` (both
junction tests) all exercised the repository-filesystem probing that no longer exists — `stats`
now never opens a file in the scanned repository, which removes that traversal surface entirely.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (also `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=linux`), `gofmt -l -s .` clean;
`go test ./... -count=1` and `go test -race ./... -count=1` green (4,951 tests);
`scripts/entire-graph-statusline_test.sh` 151/151.

Trail: perf(stats): one-line answer, and stop burning the machine to get it
  Number:  165
  ID:      01M1Q8NH2Z5A7MD3MHVWW7FAEW
  Branch:  fix/stats-fast-and-plain
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  suhaanthayyil
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/165
  Assignees: suhaanthayyil
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-09-04T22:29:43Z
  Updated: 2026-09-04T22:31:34Z

Description:
Problem:
entire graph stats analyzed session transcripts to report graph usage vs. exploration tool usage and estimated token savings. But it was slow — users with hundreds of MB of transcript logs would wait several seconds for output, because the command JSON-parsed every transcript on every run. When saving is low, verbose output was unnecessary noise for humans just wanting one number. The command also attributed savings to a theoretical whole-file read that was increasingly disconnected from reality.
Solution:
The command now has three layers of performance optimization:
Default to one line: entire graph stats --repo . prints one line — the estimated tokens saved. The --verbose flag restores the full per-verb and per-kind tables.
Per-file memoization: Unchanged transcripts are cached under the cache directory, keyed on file identity (path + size + mtime + binary version), so repeat runs on the same session transcripts skip JSON parsing entirely. --since prunes the file list by mtime before opening anything, so a --since 1d filter now runs in near-constant time on gigabyte-scale directories. The cache is transparent (--no-cache disables it); corrupt cache always falls back silently to recomputing.
Measured savings model: The savings estimate now prices from the session's own measured costs, not from a guessed repository median. Description:
Problem:
entire graph stats analyzed session transcripts to report graph usage vs. exploration tool usage and estimated token savings. But it was slow — users with hundreds of MB of transcript logs would wait several seconds for output, because the command JSON-parsed every transcript on every run. When saving is low, verbose output was unnecessary noise for humans just wanting one number. The command also attributed savings to a theoretical whole-file read that was increasingly disconnected from reality.
Solution:
The command now has three layers of performance optimization:
Default to one line: entire graph stats --repo . prints one line — the estimated tokens saved. The --verbose flag restores the full per-verb and per-kind tables.
Per-file memoization: Unchanged transcripts are cached under the cache directory, keyed on file identity (path + size + mtime + binary version), so repeat runs on the same session transcripts skip JSON parsing entirely. --since prunes the file list by mtime before opening anything, so a --since 1d filter now runs in near-constant time on gigabyte-scale directories. The cache is transparent (--no-cache disables it); corrupt cache always falls back silently to recomputing.
Measured savings model: The savings estimate now prices from the session's own measured costs, not from a guessed repository median. Each search/neighbors/impact call is credited with the one exploration call (Read/Grep/Bash) it displaced — priced as exploration_bytes_per_call - graph_bytes_per_call, both measured from this session's own transcript. A session where graph calls returned more per call than exploration contributes zero savings (correct answer, not floored away at the total).
The new JSON contract is additive only (transcripts_considered, transcripts_from_cache, graph_locate_calls, per-call cost fields, sessions_with_positive_savings, substitution_ratio); scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh reads the estimated savings and uses the memoized cost to render a status line on every prompt without blocking the user.
"}

content.text:
Reviewed [trail 165 / PR #213](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/213) at `f3cb890e`. **Three findings; I recommend changes.**

1. **[P2] Deduplication discards results from later copies.** At [stats.go:649](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/f3cb890e6d426d3bd3800f7c30b7ca9a98d08621/internal/cli/stats.go#L649), an already-seen call is skipped even when its first copy lacked a result. A reproduction with an incomplete transcript followed by a complete replay reports **0 result bytes instead of 13**. Merge result completeness while counting the call once.

2. **[P2] Partial replays overwrite complete token usage.** At [stats.go:675](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/f3cb890e6d426d3bd3800f7c30b7ca9a98d08621/internal/cli/stats.go#L675), the lexicographically last transcript wins regardless of completeness. A complete message with 50 output tokens followed by a partial replay reports **5**, distorting billed totals and savings percentages. Preserve the complete usage record independently of filename order.

3. **[P2] Cache loading skips gzip integrity validation.** At [stats_cache.go:124](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/f3cb890e6d426d3bd3800f7c30b7ca9a98d08621/internal/cli/stats_cache.go#L124), decoding one JSON value does not ensure the gzip stream reaches a valid EOF. Removing its eight-byte footer still serves **all 10 cached transcripts**, contradicting the promised corruption fallback. Validate the entire stream before accepting entries.

All three reproduced with focused tests. Existing stats tests and **151/151 status-line checks passed**. Your working tree is unchanged; no review was published.

entire session adopt — Adopt an active session from another worktree
Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository.

This is useful when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves
and makes changes in another. Adoption moves the live session state into the
current repo and seeds it with the current repo's uncommitted file changes so
the next commit can be linked normally.

When the source and target share a Git session store, adoption moves the same
session state file to the current worktree and requires --force or --yes.

      "textSnapshot": "Problem:\nentire graph stats analyzed session transcripts to report graph usage vs. exploration tool usage and estimated token savings. But it was slow — users with hundreds of MB of transcript logs would wait several seconds for output, because the command JSON-parsed every transcript on every run. When saving is low, verbose output was unnecessary noise for humans just wanting one number. The command also attributed savings to a theoretical whole-file read that was increasingly disconnected from reality.\nSolution:\nThe command now has three layers of performance optimization:\nDefault to one line: entire graph stats --repo . prints one line — the estimated tokens saved. The --verbose flag restores the full per-verb and per-kind tables.\nPer-file memoization: Unchanged transcripts are cached under the cache directory, keyed on file identity (path + size + mtime + binary version), so repeat runs on the same session transcripts skip JSON parsing entirely. --since prunes the file list by mtime before opening anything, so a --since 1d filter now runs in near-constant time on gigabyte-scale directories. The cache is transparent (--no-cache disables it); corrupt cache always falls back silently to recomputing.\nMeasured savings model: The savings estimate now prices from the session's own measured costs, not from a guessed repository median. Each search/neighbors/impact call is credited with the one exploration call (Read/Grep/Bash) it displaced — priced as exploration_bytes_per_call - graph_bytes_per_call, both measured from this session's own transcript. A session where graph calls returned more per call than exploration contributes zero savings (correct answer, not floored away at the total).\nThe new JSON contract is additive only (transcripts_considered, transcripts_from_cache, graph_locate_calls, per-call cost fields, sessions_with_positive_savings, substitution_ratio); scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh reads the estimated savings and uses the memoized cost to render a status line on every prompt without blocking the user.",

entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
